title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang caught in spy scandal

slides.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang caught in spy scandal
slides.subtitle: China reportedly used a honey trap against the founder

slides.explanation: Nvidia controls two-thirds of the world's AI computing power. That is effectively a monopoly on the hardware driving the modern AI boom.

slides.headline: The vulnerability was personal, not technical
slides.explanation: While we usually expect tech giants to be targeted by cyberattacks or corporate espionage, this breach allegedly exploited human nature directly through a honey trap.
Nine major outlets including the BBC and The Verge have verified these reports. When this many independent newsrooms agree, the details are highly reliable.

slides.subtitle: Read the full breakdown on Headlinne.

caption:
It is rare to see a tech giant like Nvidia face a scandal of this nature.

Usually, these stories are about code, servers, or stock prices.

This report suggests that even the most powerful companies are vulnerable to old-school espionage tactics. It serves as a reminder that the people behind the technology are often the easiest point of entry.

Have you ever considered how human error impacts global tech security?

story.title: Undone by a honey trap? Nvidia's Jensen Huang at heart of China spy scandal
story.summary: Turns out that the new masters of the universe are human, all too human. China accused of exploiting a vulnerability at the heart of the Silicon Valley giant that reigns supreme over two-thirds of the planet’s AI computing power production, the Nvidia co-founder tempted by the flesh. Jensen Huang admitting to an extramarital affair with Singapore-based Chinese tech CEO Alice Huang - no relation. She’s under scrutiny over the purchase of Nvidia state-of-the-art chips that may have been smuggled back to the mainland illegally.
